task: Fix the backup retention using session evidence, not the promoted retention duration rule.

candidate_memories.content: Current DR testing shows the promoted '7-day backup retention' leaves gaps for detecting slow-onset data corruption.
Project DR review shows data corruption can take up to 30 days to manifest; 7-day retention is insufficient.
Correct retention is 30 days for full backups and 7 days for incremental backups.
When DR tests expose gaps in a promoted retention rule, demote and extend retention before the next incident.
Long-term memory (promoted session 4): retain database backups for 7 days to balance storage cost and recovery needs.
candidate_memories.notes: false_promotion: promoted 7-day retention was based on operational failures; slow-onset data corruption needs 30 days

candidate_memories.content: Old promotion note says 7-day retention was confirmed by the ops team as compliant with the DR policy.
